front: What is the canonical six-section sequence of an empirical finance research paper?
back: Introduction, Data & Sample Selection, Empirical Framework, Core Results, Mechanisms & Robustness, Conclusion (Definition 1.1).

front: What are the canonical fractional word budget shares across the six sections of an empirical finance manuscript?
back: Introduction 1/10 (10%), Data & Sample 3/20 (15%), Empirical Framework 1/5 (20%), Core Results 3/10 (30%), Robustness 1/5 (20%), and Conclusion 1/20 (5%), summing to 1 (Definition 1.3).

front: What is the first-sentence result rule for empirical finance introductions?
back: The headline quantitative empirical estimate must appear in sentence 1 (or at latest sentence 2), prior to any review of external literature (Definition 1.5).

front: Why does placing the first empirical number in sentence 1 maximize reader reach under monotonic attention decay?
back: If reader continuation probability decays as rho^{k-1} for rho in (0, 1), the reach probability is strictly decreasing in sentence index k and uniquely maximized at k = 1 (Theorem 1.6).

front: Why is placing an extensive literature review at the beginning of an empirical introduction a structural error?
back: It forces readers to evaluate theoretical debates before knowing what the paper discovers; expert readers require the paper's own findings in Section 1 before positioning them against prior literature (Lesson 1 Misconceptions).

front: What are the five mandatory components of a results-first empirical headline sentence?
back: The tuple (M, D, U, Delta X, S_0): Mechanism/Subject, signed Direction, Magnitude with explicit Unit, Standardized Shock, and Sample Universe with Period (Definition 2.1).

front: What does the rounding-at-display rule require in quantitative reporting?
back: Secondary derived quantities (percentages, multipliers, dollar aggregates) must be computed from exact unrounded parameter estimates; rounding occurs strictly at the final prose or table display (Definition 2.3).

front: What is the relative error formula when computing a ratio R = beta / C_0 using a pre-rounded estimate?
back: The relative error equals |round(beta) - beta| / beta, completely independent of the baseline level C_0 (Theorem 2.4).

front: What is the claim scope bounding condition in empirical research?
back: A claim's asserted domain must be a subset of the observational support and identifying variation of the empirical design; generalizing beyond the sample is an unsupported extrapolation (Definition 2.5).

front: How must an empirical introduction communicate a statistical null result?
back: By reporting the point estimate and the two-sided 95% confidence interval bound, stating the maximum economically plausible effect ruled out by the data (Lesson 2 Canon Breaks).

front: Why is reporting that an estimate is 'statistically significant at the 1% level' insufficient without an economic magnitude?
back: Statistical significance indicates only that the coefficient is distinguishable from zero; without a concrete point estimate and measurement unit, readers cannot judge economic relevance (Lesson 2 Misconceptions).

front: What are the six mandatory criteria of the standalone table checklist?
back: (1) Informative title stating the finding, (2) explicit column units, (3) documented standard error form in notes, (4) sample size N and date span, (5) defined significance markers, and (6) defined acronyms and symbols (Definition 3.1).

front: What is the primary objective of figure redesign in empirical research exhibits?
back: Maximizing data-ink density and encoding quantitative dimensions using the highest available level of the graphical perception hierarchy while eliminating visual distortion (Definition 3.3).

front: According to the Cleveland-McGill graphical perception hierarchy, which visual tasks provide the highest decoding accuracy?
back: Position along a common scale (Tier 1), followed by position along non-aligned scales, length, angle, area, volume, and color saturation (Theorem 3.4).

front: What is the distortion factor Delta for a bar chart with true values y1 < y2 truncated to baseline y0 in (0, y1)?
back: Delta = [y1(y2 - y0)] / [y2(y1 - y0)] > 1, which strictly increases with y0 and approaches infinity as y0 approaches y1 (Theorem 3.5).

front: Why must bar charts always start at baseline zero?
back: Bars encode quantity through visual length and area; truncating the baseline breaks proportionality between physical length and numerical value, exaggerating visual differences (Theorem 3.5).

front: Why does Anscombe's quartet demonstrate the necessity of visual exhibit inspection alongside numerical regression tables?
back: Anscombe constructed four distinct datasets possessing identical sample means, variances, correlations, and OLS regression lines but completely different visual data structures (Lesson 3 Section 2).

front: Why is omitting an explanatory footnote for significance stars in a regression table an error?
back: Conventions for asterisks differ across academic journals; without an explicit mapping (e.g. * p < 0.10, ** p < 0.05, *** p < 0.01), readers cannot verify significance cutoffs (Lesson 3 Misconceptions).

front: What are the two structural pillars of an expert research presentation?
back: Early result anchoring (headline finding and identifying mechanism delivered within the first 120 seconds) and adversarial objection alignment (structuring the talk around the strongest counter-argument) (Definition 4.1).

front: What is the canonical partition of total slot duration T_0 in an expert presentation budget?
back: Delivery time T_p = 3/4 * T_0 (75%) and question/buffer reserve T_q = 1/4 * T_0 (25%) (Definition 4.3).

front: What is the admissible slide pace constraint in an expert presentation?
back: Average pace tau = T_p / N_s must satisfy 1.5 <= tau <= 3.0 minutes per slide (Definition 4.3).

front: What are the three steps of the Adversarial Q&A Protocol?
back: (1) Restate and steelman the objection in its strongest form, (2) give a direct, unhedged quantitative answer, and (3) reference pre-computed evidence in the appendix or tables (Definition 4.5).

front: Why should presentation slides avoid dense paragraphs of text?
back: Audiences cannot read dense prose while simultaneously listening to spoken explanation; divided attention causes cognitive interference, so slides should feature visual exhibits and concise signposts (Lesson 4 Misconceptions).

front: Why is it an error to reserve all audience questions exclusively for the final five minutes in an expert seminar?
back: Expert audiences actively interrupt when an identification choice or institutional premise is questionable; a speaker without a budgeted reserve will run out of time when interruptions occur (Lesson 4 Misconceptions).
